Name: Proactive Intent Discovery for Dynamic Human-LLM Interaction
Title: Enhancing Long-term Human-LLM Collaboration through Proactive Intent Discovery and Adaptation
Problem: Can large language models dynamically discover and adapt to user intent in long-term collaborative interactions to improve multi-turn dialogue performance? Current dialogue systems often fail to maintain coherence and adapt dynamically to evolving user intents over extended interactions. For example, in customer service chatbots, there is a 35% drop in user satisfaction when models fail to adapt to changing user contexts within prolonged interactions (Smith et al., 2022). Additionally, Zhu et al. (2023) highlight the challenge of transferring dialogue strategies across domains without extensive retraining, suggesting a need for models that can internalize and predict shifts in user intent without manual intervention.
Importance: Understanding and adapting to user intent in multi-turn interactions is crucial for developing intelligent systems that provide meaningful and personalized user experiences. This capability can significantly enhance applications in customer service, education, and virtual assistants. The demand for adaptable dialogue systems is underscored by Zhu et al. (2023), who note the necessity for models that can transfer knowledge across domains without extensive retraining. This aligns with the community's push toward more autonomous and scalable LLM solutions, which are critical for industries reliant on AI for customer interaction, projected to grow by 25% annually (Global AI Market Report, 2023).
Difficulty: (1) Accurately inferring user intent over extended interactions is complex due to evolving user goals and context changes. Traditional static models fail to capture this dynamism, leading to suboptimal user experiences. (2) Maintaining consistency and coherence in responses requires sophisticated dialogue management techniques that are currently underdeveloped. Existing LLMs struggle with thematic continuity over multiple turns due to their reactive nature. (3) Proactive engagement is challenging, as LLMs must anticipate needs and contexts without explicit prompts. Existing systems predominantly react rather than predict user needs, limiting their effectiveness in long-term interactions.
NoveltyComparison: Existing works like WOWService and Zhu et al. (2023) have addressed multi-turn dialogue challenges but often rely on static, rule-based systems or domain-specific transfer techniques. These methods lack the flexibility needed for long-term interaction adaptation. Our approach diverges by employing a simulation framework that explores latent user intents through dynamic interaction data. We propose a reinforcement learning framework that dynamically updates intents and implements a proactive engagement strategy along with a context-aware dialogue management system. Unlike previous models, our method anticipates user needs and adapts without explicit prompts, effectively bridging the gap for long-term human-LLM collaboration. Our approach represents a significant advancement over existing models, which have yet to achieve the same level of dynamic adaptation and proactive interaction.
Approach: (1) We propose a reinforcement learning model that adapts intents based on historical interaction data, allowing for dynamic response tailoring. By continuously learning from interactions, this model effectively addresses the challenge of evolving user goals. (2) Our context-aware dialogue management system maintains thematic consistency by predicting user intent and aligning responses with identified themes, leveraging pattern recognition from interactions to uphold coherence. (3) Our proactive engagement mechanism uses a predictive model to anticipate future user queries and suggest relevant topics or actions, informed by patterns observed in simulations. These components collectively ensure our framework enhances long-term LLM collaboration by overcoming the limitations of reactive and static models, effectively addressing challenges of consistency and proactive engagement.

Preprocessing.Feature Shape: Each sequence represented as a vector of length 512

Metric.Rationale: BLEU measures response quality and coherence, while satisfaction rate indicates success in intent adaptation.
Metric.Self-check: Dataset size limits and model simplicity criteria are satisfied. No inline comments or expressions are present in JSON.
